findings.title: Suspect-issue PR comments will crash with AttributeError
findings.body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info were added as methods of CommitContextIntegration, but GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow (subclasses of PRCommentWorkflow, which does not inherit CommitContextIntegration) call them as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue). That raises AttributeError before a comment body can be built, so merged-PR suspect-issue comments stop being posted. The helper also calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not PRCommentWorkflow, so even a direct call on the integration class fails the same way. The updated GitHub/GitLab comment tests expect the new body and will fail on this AttributeError. Move the helpers onto PRCommentWorkflow (where the callers live) and truncate via that class.

findings.title: Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
findings.body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, WidgetCardChart replaces StyledSimpleTableChart with TableWidgetVisualization passed columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. The real result.data, result.meta, fields, and loading state are discarded. TableWidgetVisualization only falls back to meta.fields when columns is nullish, so an empty array also suppresses column extraction. Enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget (including during load) instead of showing the query.

findings.title: Error context is paired by dict order, not event id
findings.body: fetch_error_details builds node ids from error_ids, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()) on the dict returned by nodestore.backend.get_multi. That pairs by iteration order, not by node id. Backends that omit missing keys (the usual get_multi behavior) shift every later row: if the second id is absent, the third event's title, message, and timestamp are attached to the second id and the last id is dropped. The id field is not even used in the log line, so the Seer prompt gets the wrong errors and timestamps. The new test only stores one error, so it cannot catch this. Look up each node id in the dict instead of zipping values().

findings.title: Error and breadcrumb timestamps are not on the same scale
findings.body: gen_request_data interleaves errors and breadcrumbs with error["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0). Replay segment events are raw rrweb records whose timestamp is epoch milliseconds. fetch_error_details copies the nodestore event timestamp, which is epoch seconds (or sometimes an ISO string). Seconds are always less than millisecond breadcrumbs, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb and the summary chronology is wrong for real replays. An ISO-string timestamp raises TypeError on < or sort, and that exception is outside fetch_error_details's try/except, so the summarize request 500s. The new tests hide this by writing segment JSON with now.timestamp() seconds. Normalize both sides to the same numeric unit before comparing.

findings.title: Error ids are queried with the page stats window, not the replay
findings.body: Error context now depends on query_replay_instance(start=filter_params["start"], end=filter_params["end"]) from ProjectEndpoint.get_filter_params. The replay AI tab (static/app/views/replays/detail/ai/index.tsx) calls this endpoint with no start, end, or statsPeriod. The lookup therefore uses the generic project default stats window rather than the replay's own start/end. Replays outside that window return no row, error_ids stays empty, and the summary is produced without error context with no error to the user. Query the replay by id over its retention window, or pass the replay bounds from the client.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. When the search box is empty the code returns sortAttributes(attributes) unchanged, so those internal fields stay visible. Once the user types a query that would match them, they disappear. If the intent is to hide them, filter them out before the search check; otherwise search results disagree with the full list.

findings.title: Feedback list is clipped after the summary is inserted
findings.body: The list grid cell used to be a FluidHeight Container (height 100% of the stretched grid area). It is now SummaryListContainer, a column flex with no min-height: 0 or overflow handling, containing FeedbackSummary plus that same height-100% Container. The list's 100% height is the full cell, then the summary and gap are added on top, so the column overflows the grid row. Background and LayoutGrid both set overflow: hidden, so the bottom of the feedback list is clipped and no longer lines up with the details pane. Give the list container flex: 1 and min-height: 0 (and overflow: hidden) so it fills only the space under the summary.

findings.title: Attribute-key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
findings.body: useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always reduce the API payload to a TagCollection (empty object if data was missing) and return that once loading finished. It now returns useQuery's data directly: attributes is previous while isFetching, otherwise data. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and there is no ?? {}. Explore callers that wait for !isLoading and then spread or Object.keys the result will throw, blanking the search builder, instead of seeing an empty tag set. Return data ?? {} (and keep the previous value only while refetching).

findings.title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
findings.body: useFeedbackSummary reads usePageFilters().selection and sends normalized datetime plus project, but not selection.environments. The feedback list on the same page is scoped by the environment page filter. With an environment selected, the summary is computed from every environment in the projects and date range, so it can describe feedback the list is not showing. Pass environment (and any other page filters the summary API supports) in the query.

findings.title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity auth refresh
findings.body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while it still loops up to chunk_size (default 100) identities, each doing an org-membership RPC and provider.refresh_identity HTTP call. 100 sequential IdP calls routinely exceed 60s, so the taskworker kills the task mid-batch. check_auth already sets last_synced=now on those ids before enqueueing this task, and they are not selected again until the next ~24h window (AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL). Identities not yet refreshed are skipped for a day, so SSO invalidation is delayed. Raise the deadline to match the chunk, or shrink the chunk to what 60s can finish.

findings.title: Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized
findings.body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE is "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n" and _truncate_title only slices to 50 characters. Issue titles come from user-influenced error messages. A title containing ] or ) breaks out of the link, for example [**click here](https://evil.example)**](real-url), and is posted to GitHub/GitLab. Truncation does not stop that. Escape markdown metacharacters in the title (and backticks in the environment name) before formatting.

findings.title: Report age/timestamp rules do not match the spec the serializer claims
findings.body: age and timestamp are both required=False, and there is no object-level validate() requiring exactly one of them. A report with neither is accepted and counted. The field validators also use initial_data.get("age") / get("timestamp"), which treat 0 as absent, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 skips both mutual-exclusion checks (0 is a valid age and a valid timestamp). Use "age" in initial_data (and the same for timestamp) and reject payloads that do not have exactly one of the two fields.
